$comment: ANTI-mirror map for backend/space <-> frontend/lib/space (openspec:
add-space-kinematics, design.md Decision 1 — Go is the SOLE authority for
continuous-space kinematics and there is no TypeScript mirror, now or later;
cross-stack-determinism › 'A Go-sole-authority capability's mirror map runs in
anti-mirror mode').
This file is the INVERSE of fixtures/board/mirror-map.json and
fixtures/polar/mirror-map.json. Those assert a mirror EXISTS and is covered.
This one asserts a mirror does NOT exist: .claude/scripts/check-mirror-map.sh's
anti_mirror_space pass fails if any function name is declared in BOTH
backend/space and frontend/lib/space unless it is listed in 'sharedNames'.
There is deliberately no 'pairs' array — a pairs entry would assert the very
mirror this capability exists to forbid.
'sharedNames' is empty BY DEFAULT and should stay that way. Adding a name here
is a claim that a render-side function may legitimately share a name with an
authoritative Go one; it needs the same scrutiny as a spec change.
frontend/lib/space does not exist as of this change (tasks.md 2.2 records that
omission as deliberate: the Go package has zero consumers, so there is no render
surface yet to draw). frontend/app/spike/space-3d is NEVER scanned — it is the
exempt, non-shipping feel bench named in space-kinematics › 'Every Rule-Bearing
Value of This Capability Is Computed Only in the Authoritative Implementation'.
'coverage' below is this capability's COVERAGE INVENTORY (tasks.md 3.9): every
function declared in backend/space, reconciled against the fixture families in
fixtures/space/cases.json. Values: 'family:<name>' — asserted by that family,
directly or indirectly as a callee of the family's function; 'inventory' — no
family exercises it, tracked as a gap in 'inventory' below.

inventory.why: The Firestore/action.Params codec is a persistence boundary, not a geometry function: its outputs are storage-native primitives and its failures are named sentinels, neither of which a byte-for-byte float family adds anything to. It is covered by backend/space/params_test.go across the accepted int/int64/float64 arrival shapes and the non-finite / out-of-extent rejections.
inventory.expectedChange: the first change that gives backend/space a consumer — at which point a stored round trip crosses a real Firestore document and a fixture family earns its keep

inventory.why: Upkeep is a closed-form product of a body-derived rate and elapsed world time, unit-tested in park_test.go (the floor, the ordering of an inner vs an outer body, and read-count independence over 500 sub-intervals). No family sweeps it because nothing consumes a station-keep charge yet.
inventory.expectedChange: the change that introduces a delta-v or credit consumer for station-keeping — the first point at which the rate becomes a rule-bearing stored value rather than a computable one

inventory.why: Covered by three hand-selected parkPosition cases (the (3,2,4) planar re-circularization, the directly-above minimum-radius case, and the released park evaluated later) but by no randomized sweep, so an offset distribution it mishandles could still hide.
inventory.expectedChange: the change that first lets a player release a station-keep hold

inventory.why: A thin wrapper over minDistanceAndParamOf, retained for readability and currently called only by tests. Its companion IS swept via buildCurve's star-clearance axis.
inventory.expectedChange: delete it, or give it a caller, in the change that first migrates a consumer onto backend/space
